To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated and characterized a large number of natural epothilons and related compounds from Sorangium cellsulsum, strains So ce 90/B2 and D13, that we have determined the structure of these compounds, and that we have established structure-activity relationships for these compounds.
the new epothilinone variants are produced in low yields, and the new compounds do not exceed the activity of epothilone A (1) in cytotoxicity assays.

we have isolated and characterized 37 novel epothilone derivatives and epothilon-related compounds from the fermentation broth of the myxobacterium Sorangium celluosum, strain So 90/B2, and that these compounds are the result of the incomplete selectivity of the enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of epothilones for the acetate and propionates used in the synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and structural elucidation of 37 natural epo thilones, the first 18-membered ring macrolides, and the first ring-contrac ted 14-membered ring epothilones, and their SAR studies.
the isolation and structure elucidation of new epothilonic compounds from S. cellulosum, and with structure-activity relationships of the new compounds.
the elucidation of the biosynthesis of epothilones and with the identification of new epothilonic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epothilones are not a family of natural products, but rather a single family of closely related natural compounds.
the new natural epothileones show a similar cytotoxicity as epothilone B (2), but in no case exceed its activity.

the epothilone biosynthetic pathway is very robust and flexible, and the enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of epothilones are very promiscuous, which is reflected by the large number of epothilone derivatives found in the natural product extracts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, with respect to epothilone A, the most active natural epothilomes are the 12-deoxy-12-methylene (1), the 12-deoxymethyl (14) and the 12-deacetoxy (15) compounds, which are produced in amounts of 1-6 mg/L.

epothilones are a very versatile class of compounds with respect to their structural diversity and biological activity, but that they do not represent a class of drugs with a broad therapeutic spectrum.
epothilones with an unsaturated 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl side chain are the best candidates for the development of new anticancer drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosynthetic machinery of S. cellulosum is not very selective, which is in contrast to the high degree of selectivity of the enzymes of other polyketide-producing organisms.
the biosynthetic machinery of Sorangium can be directed to produce a variety of epothilone-like macrolides, which are all active as cytostatic agents.
the epothilone biosynthesis is very versatile and that the producing organism is able to cope with a variety of biosynthetic errors.
